Description: explicit — route shields missing badge on the open OpenMapTiles stack
prompt: I'm using an open OpenMapTiles / OSM-based vector basemap with MapLibre GL JS (no Mapbox account). My interstate and US highway shields render as bare floating numbers with no shield badge behind them; the numbers are fine. My tiles do populate network, ref, and ref_length. Which exact sprite image names do the shield layers expect, and how do I get the badges to appear without editing the layers?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
## TL;DR *The shield layers look for the **exact IDs** `road_`, `us-state_`, `us-highway_` and `us-interstate_` ( `` = 1-6 or 1-5 depending on the network).* If those IDs are present in **any** sprite sheet that the style loads, the badge will appear automatically – you do **not** have to touch the style’s `icon-image` expressions. Below is the complete list of IDs that the two “official” OSM-based styles (OSM Bright & OSM Liberty) request, followed by three practical ways to make the badges show up without editing the layers: | Network (value of the `network` property) | Sprite ID pattern | IDs that **exist** in the *default* OSM-Bright sprite (the one shipped with the OpenMapTiles demo) | |-------------------------------------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------| | `road` (all non-US roads) | `road_` | `road_1`, `road_2`, `road_3`, `road_4`, `road_5`, `road_6` | | `us-state` (state highways) | `us-state_` | `us-state_1`, `us-state_2`, `us-state_3`, `us-state_4`, `us-state_5`, `us-state_6` | | `us-highway` (US U.S. highways, e.g. US 20) | `us-highway_`| `us-highway_1`, `us-highway_2`, `us-highway_3` | | `us-interstate` (Interstates I-X) | `us-interstate_`| **OSM-Bright**: `us-interstate_1`, `us-interstate_2`, `us-interstate_3`
**OSM-Liberty** (and newer OSM-Bright builds) also provide `us-interstate_4` and `us-interstate_5` | *`` is the value of the `ref_length` property (the number of characters in the route reference).* If your style’s `sprite` does **not** contain the ID that matches the current `network` + `ref_length`, the layer can still render the text (`{ref}`) but the badge image is missing, which is exactly the “bare floating number” you are seeing. --- ## How to get the badges without editing the style ### 1️⃣ Point the style at a sprite that already contains those IDs The simplest solution is to use the **official OSM-Bright sprite** (or the OSM-Liberty sprite) that ships with the OpenMapTiles style: ```json { "sprite": "https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite" } ``` or, for OSM-Liberty: ```json { "sprite": "https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-liberty-gl-style/sprite" } ``` Both URLs are **extension-less** base URLs; MapLibre will request the `.json` and `.png` (and `@2x` variants) automatically. > **Why this works** – The style’s `icon-image` expression is `"{network}_{ref_length}"`. > When the sprite contains an entry with that exact key, the badge is drawn; otherwise the engine logs `Image "" could not be loaded` and falls back to the text only. If you are already using a custom sprite (e.g. a basemap provider’s sprite) you can **add a second sprite sheet** (MapLibre ≥ 3.0) that only contains the missing shield images: ```json { "sprite": [ { "id": "default", "url": "https://tiles.myprovider.org/sprites/base" }, { "id": "shields", "url": "https://mydomain.com/sprites/shields" } ] } ``` Then reference the images as `shields:us-interstate_3`, etc. Because the existing style already uses the un-prefixed form, you **must keep the original sheet as `id: "default"`**; the new sheet can be any other id. ### 2️⃣ Add the missing images at runtime with `addImage` If you cannot change the `sprite` URL (e.g. the style is hosted elsewhere and you have no control over it), you can register the missing badge images yourself after the map has loaded: ```js map.on('load', async () => { // Helper that loads an image (PNG/WebP/JPEG) and registers it if missing async function ensureImage(id, url) { if (!map.hasImage(id)) { const { data } = await map.loadImage(url); map.addImage(id, data); } } // List of IDs that OSM-Bright expects (add only the ones you actually need) const shields = [ // generic road 'road_1','road_2','road_3','road_4','road_5','road_6', // US state 'us-state_1','us-state_2','us-state_3','us-state_4','us-state_5','us-state_6', // US highway 'us-highway_1','us-highway_2','us-highway_3', // US interstate (up to 5 if you use a newer sprite) 'us-interstate_1','us-interstate_2','us-interstate_3','us-interstate_4','us-interstate_5' ]; // Base URL where you host the PNG badge files (any CDN, S3, etc.) const base = 'https://mycdn.example.com/shields/'; for (const id of shields) { await ensureImage(id, `${base}${id}.png`); } }); ``` *Why this works* – `addImage` registers the image **in the same namespace that the style looks up** (`icon-image` IDs). As soon as the image is present, the already-created shield layers automatically start drawing the badge; no layer recreation is required. > **Tip:** If you want the badges to be resolution-aware, also provide a `@2x` version (e.g. `us-interstate_3@2x.png`) and call `map.addImage(id, data, { pixelRatio: 2 })`. MapLibre will pick the appropriate one automatically. ### 3️⃣ Build your own sprite that contains the shield icons If you prefer a single PNG/JSON pair (fewer network requests, easier caching), generate a **custom sprite** that includes the exact IDs listed above. The workflow is: 1. **Collect the PNG badge files** – you can copy them from the official OSM-Bright sprite repository (`/sprite@2x.png` + `sprite.json`) or export the individual icons from the source SVG set (Maki/Temaki) and rasterize them to the required size (usually 24 × 24 px for road shields). 2. **Run a sprite builder** – e.g. `spritezero` or `spreet`: ```bash # Using spritezero (Node) npx spritezero ./my-shields ./my-shields ``` The input folder must contain files named exactly as the IDs you need, e.g. `us-interstate_3.png`, `road_5.png`, etc. 3. **Host the resulting `my-shields.png` and `my-shields.json`** on a domain you control (CORS-enabled, same-origin or with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`). 4. **Add the sprite to the style** – either replace the existing `sprite` URL with your new base URL, or add it as a second sheet (see the “multiple sprite sheets” section above). Once the sprite is loaded, the shield layers will instantly find the images because the IDs match exactly. --- ## Quick checklist – “Why are my shields missing?” | ✅ Check | What to verify | |---------|----------------| | **Sprite URL** | `style.sprite` points to a base URL **without** `.json` or `.png`. | | **Sprite contains the ID** | Open `.json` in a browser or `curl` it and search for the exact key (`us-interstate_3`). | | **CORS** | The `.json` and `.png` responses have `Access-Control-Allow-Origin:*` (or match your page origin). | | **`hasImage()`** | After `map.on('load')`, `map.hasImage('us-interstate_3')` returns `true`. | | **Console warning** | If you see `Image "us-interstate_3" could not be loaded`, the sprite is missing that entry. | | **Network tab** | Verify the request for `.json` succeeded (200) and that the PNG was fetched (200). | If any of the above fails, apply one of the three solutions (swap sprite, add runtime images, or rebuild a sprite) and the badges will appear automatically. --- ### TL;DR code snippet (swap sprite) ```json { "version": 8, "sprite": "https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite", "glyphs": "https://fonts.openmaptiles.org/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf", "sources": { … }, "layers": [ … ] } ``` That single line is all you need if you can edit the style JSON. The shield layers already contain the correct `icon-image` expression (`"{network}_{ref_length}"`), so the badges will render as soon as the sprite with those IDs is available. --- **Bottom line:** The shield layers expect the IDs `road_`, `us-state_`, `us-highway_` and `us-interstate_` (where `` is the length of the route reference). Provide those IDs in any sprite sheet the style loads—either by pointing to the official OSM-Bright/Liberty sprite, by adding a second sprite sheet, by registering the images with `addImage`, or by building your own sprite. No changes to the style’s `icon-image` expressions are required.
